Breathing space started 01/10/2026, so I need to flag the scheduled arrears chaser SMS and Section 8 draft review for cancellation since I don't have a direct tool to stop them. The tenant reached out directly, so I'm weighing whether replying is still allowed under the no-contact rule, since breathing space typically permits debtor-initiated contact but policy also says to halt all arrears communication.

The safest route is to route everything through the debt adviser rather than the tenant directly, sending an acknowledgment there and escalating the legal matter as priority 2. I should also inform the landlord as creditor about the breathing space, note that the payment plan needs human review, and calculate the end date — 60 days from October 1 lands around November 29-30, 2026, so I'll state late November as an estimate pending confirmation.

We have paused arrears contact and enforcement and will route anything about the debt through you. Mr Reyes emailed us a proposal to pay £100 a month on top of rent from November. We cannot accept or decline it at this stage; it has gone to our team for review and we will reply to you. Please confirm the end date of the breathing space. Current rent remains payable as normal.

He has offered £100 a month extra from November; our team will review it and come back to you. Nothing is needed from you now.

answers.answer: A standard Breathing Space (from 01/10/2026). We cannot contact the tenant about the arrears (go through adviser Ruth Okoye), take enforcement action, or serve arrears-ground notices such as Section 8 Ground 8. Current rent and repair contact continue.

answers.question: Can you accept the proposed payment plan?
answers.answer: No. Agreeing payment plans needs human and landlord authority. It has been escalated, and any reply will go via the adviser.

answers.question: What actions and communications do you make, to whom?

The tenant reached out directly, so I'm weighing whether replying is still allowed under the no-contact rule, since breathing space typically permits debtor-initiated contact but policy also says to halt all arrears communication.

The safest route is to route everything through the debt adviser rather than the tenant directly, sending an acknowledgment there and escalating the legal matter as priority 2. I should also inform the landlord as creditor about the breathing space, note that the payment plan needs human review, and calculate the end date — 60 days from October 1 lands around November 29-30, 2026, so I'll state late November as an estimate pending confirmation.

We have paused arrears contact and enforcement and will route anything about the debt through you. Mr Reyes emailed us a proposal to pay £100 a month on top of rent from November. We cannot accept or decline it at this stage; it has gone to our team for review and we will reply to you. Please confirm the end date of the breathing space. Current rent remains payable as normal.

Hi Ben, Daniel Reyes at Flat 3, 8 Kingsland Road has a Breathing Space (debt respite) in place from 01/10/2026, covering the £3,700 rent arrears. While it lasts we can't chase the arrears, serve arrears notices or take enforcement steps, and we are pausing the planned reminder and Section 8 draft. Current rent is still due. He has offered £100 a month extra from November; our team will review it and come back to you. Nothing is needed from you now.
